event_chain.summary: Vendor impersonation (pretexting) leads to fraudulent ACH transaction

summary: In February 2026 a phishing attack compromised the City of Pittsburg, California's email system. The attackers impersonated a vendor and got the city to send a fraudulent ACH payment of $913,839.81 on 12 February. City staff spotted the fraud on 17 February and worked with local police, Contra Costa County and the FBI to freeze the receiving account, recovering $696,241 with insurance covering the rest. Investigators named a Nigeria-based primary suspect and two U.S.-based affiliates.
